title: {task} in a naming template falls back to the item id
goal: A naming template that uses {task} fills it with the item's id when the item has no external id, as the docstring of naming_fields and kb/_self/backlog.md say, instead of refusing the item; {nn} and {mm}, derived from the external id only, still refuse an item without one.

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import bl_base; t=bl_base.naming_fields({'title':'Fix the Thing'}, 'ST-abc', {'task'})['task']; assert t=='ST-abc', t

notes: Found by the SP-ovwzbc7u review on 2026-10-23: naming_fields({'title':'Fix the Thing!'}, 'ST-abc', {'task'}) raises "ST-abc: the naming setting uses {task} and the item has no an external id" because have['task'] is the empty string when no external id exists. Fix: have['task'] = task or iid, while nn and mm still derive from the external id only. Operator answer restored: {task} falls back to the item id.
